text:
kevin: quick sync — we need to lock down the OTel -> Prom mappings for runtime metrics before the next dashboard rollout. small scope: routing/queue/exec paths + per-route latency/errrate. can we do a short alignment today?

maria: +1. especially need rules for model and route labels. current drafts add model_id and customer_id as labels which will explode cardinality.

jasmin: agree. customer identifiers must not be high-card labels. propose we only expose customer_tier (free/pro/senterprise) and a hashed customer_bucket (8-bit) if needed for sampling/segmentation.

alex: re: model label — we should standardize on "redwood.model.name" (OTel) -> prometheus label model_name with normalized values (e.g., redwood-13b, redwood-70b-q4). avoid variant-level proliferation (quantized/float) in the label; use model_variant as separate low-card enum where needed.

sam_product: from product side: dashboards want to slice by route, model and region. region is safe. route should be normalized (use http.route if present, else fallback to route_id).

kevin: proposed mapping (OTel attr -> Prom label):
```
http.route -> route
redwood.model.name -> model_name
redwood.model.variant -> model_variant
cloud.region -> region
redwood.customer.tier -> customer_tier
redwood.customer.bucket -> customer_bucket
status -> status_code_class   # map 2xx/4xx/5xx
```
This keeps model and route accessible while controlling customer-cardinality.

maria: + the "status_code_class" should be derived server-side, not a freeform status label. we'll implement conversion in runtime exporter.

jasmin: cardinality targets we discussed: route <= 200, model_name <= 30, model_variant <= 10, region <= 10, customer_bucket <= 256, customer_tier <= 5. Are we all good with those?

alex: sounds reasonable. we also need to define which attributes go to the resource vs metric labels. e.g., customer_id should be a resource attribute (for traces/logs) and never a prometheus label.

kevin: yep. action: eng-runtime to change exporter to follow mapping; eng-platform to update dashboard templates and templating variables to use the new labels; eng-infra to run a prometheus label-cardinality check during canary.

jasmin: will add a lint rule in the metrics schema repo to flag any metric with label names matching /customer_id|user_id|email/ — block PRs unless approved.

maria: one more: sampling policy. for high-volume routes we want to enable prefix KV caching metrics only on sampled spans to avoid explosion. Recommend 1% overall sampling, 10% for e2e-flagged routes.

alex: for dashboards UX, include a top-level route selector that defaults to the top 10 by QPS, not an unscoped wildcard. avoids accidental huge queries.

sam_product: timeline? we need this in staging dashboards by next Tuesday ideally for the canary rollout.

kevin: timeline:
- today: agree mapping + owners (this thread)
- by Fri: eng-runtime PR to exporter + unit tests (owner: jasmin)
- Mon: infra run cardinality scan against staging metrics (owner: alex)
- Tue: eng-platform update dashboard templates, product review (owner: kevin/sam_product)
- Wed: small canary rollout to 5% traffic, monitor labels and cardinality (sre-bot will post alerts)

jasmin: I'll start the PR today. will include a test harness that emits synthetic labels and verifies cardinalities.

alex: i'll wire the infra check and add a PrometheusRule to alert if any label exceeds 5k series during canary.

sre-bot: scheduled: cardinality-check job will run at 2026-03-22T09:00Z and post results to #eng-platform.

maria: can we also add a short doc snippet showing how to pick between model_name vs model_variant for dashboarding? new hires keep confusing them.

kevin: good call — i'll add a small section in the metrics handbook and link it from the dashboard templates.

sam_product: thanks all. if nobody objects, i'll book 30m follow-up Wed after canary start to review telemetry and make any quick label tweaks. :thumbsup:

jasmin: no objections.

alex: fine by me.

kevin: cool, closing the loop here. owners: jasmin (exporter PR), alex (cardinality checks), kevin/sam_product (dash templates & docs). I'll post an RFC summary later in #eng-platform.

maria: :eyes: watching the PR.

sre-bot: alert: cardinality-scan scheduled job completed (staging). results: top offending label=route (820 distinct), model_name=12, customer_bucket=128. Recommendation: trim route variants (normalize query params, strip session ids).

kevin: thanks bot — jasmin/alex please triage route normalization next week.

jasmin: adding a route-normalizer step to the runtime exporter that strips known ephemeral segments and canonicalizes IDs. will include a small regex whitelist for exceptions.

maria: nice. once normalized, we should be under the 200 route target per environment.

kevin: perfect. we'll reconvene after the canary review. thanks everyone.
